title: ISP Industrial Attachment Networking Notes
description: Documented practical networking experience from OneSky Communications Ltd., including router configuration, VLANs, DHCP/NAT, IP addressing, subnetting, monitoring, and troubleshooting.
objective: Connect academic networking knowledge with real ISP operations and CCNA preparation.
steps: Observed and practiced router configuration workflows.
Reviewed VLAN, DHCP, NAT, and IP addressing use in a service provider environment.
Practiced troubleshooting customer and internal network issues.
Documented tools, commands, and lessons learned from industrial training.
learning: This project shows real-world exposure to ISP networking and explains how CCNA topics appear in operational environments.

title: CCNA Preparation Lab Series
description: A structured lab series for CCNA topics including subnetting, switching, VLANs, inter-VLAN routing, static routing, DHCP, NAT, and troubleshooting.
objective: Build exam-ready understanding through repeatable hands-on labs instead of only reading theory.
steps: Create Packet Tracer labs by CCNA topic.
Write topology, addressing table, configuration notes, and verification steps.
Test connectivity with ping, traceroute, routing table checks, and packet inspection.
Record mistakes and fixes for future revision.
learning: This project organizes CCNA preparation into portfolio-ready evidence of routing and switching practice.

title: Home Network Documentation and Security Review
description: Mapped a small home network, documented IP ranges, connected devices, router settings, and basic security improvements.
objective: Understand how a real small network is organized and practice writing clear network documentation.
steps: Listed network devices and connection types.
Recorded private IP range, gateway, DNS, and DHCP scope.
Created a simple topology diagram.
Reviewed Wi-Fi name, password strength, router admin access, and guest network settings.
learning: This project connects theory with a real environment. It shows subnetting, gateway, DHCP, wireless security, and documentation skills in one practical example.

title: Packet Tracer Two-LAN Routing Lab
description: Built two separate LANs connected by a router and verified that devices could communicate across subnets.
objective: Practice IP addressing, default gateways, router interfaces, and basic connectivity testing.
steps: Created two LANs with PCs, switches, and one router.
Configured router interfaces as gateways for each LAN.
Tested local and cross-network pings, then documented troubleshooting steps.
learning: The lab makes routing visible. It helped me understand why devices in different subnets need a gateway.

title: VLAN Segmentation Lab
description: Designed a switch lab with separate student, admin, and guest VLANs to understand traffic separation.
objective: Learn why VLANs are used and how access ports and trunk ports behave in a small network.
steps: Created VLAN 10, VLAN 20, and VLAN 30.
Assigned access ports to different VLANs.
Configured a trunk link between switches.
Tested which devices could communicate before and after routing was added.
learning: This project shows how one physical switch can support multiple logical networks and why segmentation matters.

title: Wireshark DNS Traffic Analysis
description: Captured DNS traffic and explained how a domain name is resolved into an IP address.
objective: Practice packet capture, display filters, and protocol analysis.
steps: Started a capture on the active network interface.
Used the dns display filter to reduce noise.
Visited safe websites and observed DNS queries and responses.
Documented query name, response address, and packet flow.
learning: The project helped me see that DNS is not only a theory topic. It is visible in packet captures and useful for troubleshooting.

title: Nmap Local Network Discovery Lab
description: Used Nmap in a safe local lab to discover live hosts and identify open services.
objective: Learn responsible scanning and understand what open ports can reveal about a system.
steps: Defined a lab-only target range.
Ran host discovery to identify active machines.
Scanned selected lab hosts for open ports.
Compared scan results with expected services.
learning: This project shows the difference between scanning responsibly in a lab and scanning systems without permission. It also builds service recognition skills.

title: Linux Networking Commands Cheat Sheet
description: Created a practical reference for Linux commands used during networking and cybersecurity labs.
objective: Build confidence using the Linux terminal for IP checks, connectivity tests, DNS checks, and log review.
steps: Grouped commands by purpose.
Tested commands such as ip addr, ping, traceroute, ss, and dig.
Added example outputs and notes about what each command proves.
Converted the notes into a clean README.
learning: The project turns repeated terminal practice into a reusable study resource for future labs.

title: Firewall Rules Lab
description: A small lab for allowing and blocking traffic by port, source, and destination.
objective: Understand firewall logic and the idea of least privilege.
steps: Create a test service on a lab machine.
Allow only the required port.
Block unnecessary inbound traffic.
Verify behavior with connection tests and packet captures.
learning: This project will help explain why firewall rules need a clear purpose and how overly open rules increase risk.

title: Cybersecurity Home Lab Setup
description: Built a small isolated virtual lab for practicing Linux, scanning, logging, and safe security exercises.
objective: Create a repeatable environment for learning without touching real production systems.
steps: Created isolated virtual network settings.
Installed Linux VMs for workstation and target practice.
Took snapshots before risky changes.
Documented VM names, IP addresses, and tool versions.
learning: The lab supports long-term practice and gives structure to future portfolio write-ups.

title: Phishing Awareness Checklist
description: Created a practical checklist for reviewing suspicious messages safely.
objective: Explain phishing indicators in a way non-experts and new learners can understand.
steps: Listed common warning signs such as urgency, mismatched links, and suspicious attachments.
Created a safe review process that avoids clicking unknown links.
Added examples of what to document during analysis.
Wrote a clear security awareness guide.
learning: This project shows communication skill, which matters in cybersecurity because users need clear guidance.

title: Static Cybersecurity Portfolio Website
description: Built this GitHub Pages-compatible portfolio to document learning, blogs, projects, and contact information.
objective: Create a personal brand while keeping the site simple, fast, and fully static.
steps: Built pages with HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript.
Separated blog metadata into JSON.
Created reusable navbar and footer components.
Designed a responsive dark theme with subtle terminal-inspired UI.
learning: This project proves frontend fundamentals, static deployment understanding, content organization, and long-term portfolio planning.
